🇲🇽🚆 <u>Querétaro–Saltillo Train: First 68 km Awarded for 22.4 Billion Pesos</u>

Mexico's train agency ATTRAPI awarded Mota-Engil the design and construction of the first 68 km of the Querétaro–Saltillo passenger train, from Querétaro to San Miguel de Allende, for 22.41 billion pesos. That beat ICA's 23.72 billion bid among six offers. Work starts October 17 with a 973-day deadline, covering viaducts, tunnels, stations and bridges for trains running at up to 177 km/h, El Economista reports.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PRI's Quijano Handed 114 Million Pesos to Sister Companies</u>

As PRI mayor of Magdalena Contreras (2021-2024), Luis Gerardo Quijano channeled more than 114 million pesos to three companies (Mazare Construcciones, Tenedora Inmobiliaria Vacacional and Bayca Obras y Proyectos) run by the same two business partners. Together they won at least 46 contracts through simulated tenders, direct awards and bids with no rivals. Mexico's public works law bars companies that share partners or legal representatives from bidding against each other.

🇲🇽✊ <u>Mexico's Independent Union Takes the Letelier-Moffitt Award</u>

The Liga Sindical Obrera Mexicana, an independent union organizing plants along the North American supply chain since 2021, receives the 2026 Letelier-Moffitt Human Rights Award in Washington on October 8. No Mexican union has used the T-MEC's Rapid Response Labor Mechanism more often to force transnationals to respect workers' right to organize. The award honors Orlando Letelier and Ronni Moffitt, murdered by Pinochet's agents at Sheridan Circle in 1976. Its 50th edition goes to Mexican workers.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Anti-Corruption Ministry Sanctions 55 Officials, Fines Total 102 Million Pesos</u>

Mexico's Anti-Corruption and Good Government Secretariat sanctioned 55 public servants and one company across 19 federal agencies, including Pemex, CFE, IMSS, the National Guard and Banco del Bienestar. The fines add up to about 102 million pesos. The offenses: paying for purchases that were never delivered, improper charges, sexual harassment and misuse of public resources. Thirteen officials were fired and barred from public office for ten years by the federal administrative court.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexican Phone Exports Up 30.7% in Seven Months</u>

Mexico exported $12.384 billion in telephone equipment, including smartphones and wireless network gear, from January to July 2026, up 30.7% from a year earlier, El Economista reports from INEGI data. In 2025 Mexico ranked as the world's 7th-largest exporter of these devices, with a record $17.783 billion, per the WTO. The weak spot is still the one the government is targeting: heavy reliance on imported components and thin local supplier networks.

🇲🇽🇻🇪 <u>Nine Months On, Mexico City Demands: Free Maduro</u>

At Mexico City's Monumento a la Revolución, the Mexican Coordinating Committee in Solidarity with Venezuela marked nine months since US forces seized President Nicolás Maduro and lawmaker Cilia Flores at Fuerte Tiuna in Caracas on January 3. They also demanded an end to the blockade and the return of Venezuela's seized assets. "We join the Venezuelan people in their brave demand for the immediate and unconditional freedom of their leadership," said Irma Sofía Nava. The couple are still held in New York, with trial set for June 1, 2027.

🇲🇽✊ <u>Brugada: "Mexico Is Nobody's Backyard"</u>

Delivering her second annual report at the Auditorio Nacional, Mexico City head of government Clara Brugada called for closing ranks behind President Sheinbaum against a "global gang or mafia" with tentacles in Mexico's far right, a direct shot at PAN and PRI politicians who have asked Washington to intervene militarily. Her numbers: over 300,000 square meters turned into new Utopías serving more than 2 million people, 32 more built or underway this year, and a model already exported to Quito.

🇲🇽🌧️ <u>Matamoros Floods: Mexico's Navy Activates Plan Marina on the Border</u>

Mexico's Navy activated the prevention phase of Plan Marina in Matamoros, Tamaulipas, after more than 215 millimeters of rain (8.5 inches) fell on the city between October 2 and the morning of October 4. A mobile support brigade with rescue vehicles and equipment deployed from the Matamoros Naval Sector, working alongside Civil Protection, firefighters and the Defense Ministry as State Guard units patrolled flooded neighborhoods like La Joya, Buenavista and Constituyentes.

🇲🇽📊 <u>INEGI: Fewer Children, More Income per Household — For Now</u>

Mexico's fertility rate fell from 1.9 children per woman in 2019 to 1.2 in 2024, according to INEGI's 2025 Intercensal Survey. INEGI president Graciela Márquez says the pandemic sped up a decline nobody expected to be this fast. With fewer mouths per household, income stretches further, and income poverty fell from 50.8% to 35.4% between 2018 and 2024. The catch INEGI flags: fewer young earners and more elderly down the road, which is exactly why the pension and care systems being built now matter.

🇲🇽🌎 "In 1913, generals of the old Porfirian army, together with the ambassador of the United States, promoted a coup d'état that ended the constitutional government and the lives of Madero and Pino Suárez." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, 205th anniversary of the Mexican Navy, Veracruz She traced the history of Mexico's armed forces: the Republic's 1867 victory over the French-imposed empire, the 1913 coup, and the Constitutionalist Army that defeated Huerta and opened the way to the 1917 Constitution. "We are a sovereign nation, and we have the right to decide our destiny for ourselves." The ambassador was Henry Lane Wilson; the Pact of the Embassy was signed at the US embassy in February 1913.
